note: All four authoritative full-text sources are current-run active carriers from batches 76 and 79. Their successful retrieval attempts and fetch stamps are reused, the relevant full-text sections were inspected, and source-fetch-check --stamp will revalidate the exact stored stamps. No source retrieval failed or was dropped. Source context is not used as a proof substitute; the PHS03 readiness and AC_omega gaps are recorded in batch-80 notes and cross-batch rows.

candidate_dispositions.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6
candidate_dispositions.locator: Complete 46-page review; §2, PDF pp. 6–10, on stationary black-hole mechanics and the classical-versus-thermodynamic distinction; §3, PDF pp. 10–16, on the added quantum-field assumptions behind Hawking radiation.

candidate_dispositions.title: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Introduction to black hole thermodynamics, lecture notes for the Roberto Salmeron School in Mathematical Physics (2025), arXiv:2512.24929v1
candidate_dispositions.locator: Complete 84-page lecture notes; §1.3, PDF pp. 14–16, and §2.1, PDF pp. 18–20, for the mechanical first law, the separate thermodynamic identification, and the initially unspecified area-entropy coefficient.

candidate_dispositions.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333 Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 20
candidate_dispositions.locator: Complete 15-page lecture PDF; photon-gas section, equations VI.49–VI.61 (PDF pp. 12–14; printed pp. 128–131), for two-polarization modes, Bose occupations, Planck energy density, continuum spectrum, and c/4 one-sided angular flux.

candidate_dispositions.title: University of Mississippi PHY 727 course notes, Lecture 18: The Photon Gas
candidate_dispositions.locator: Complete two-page lecture note; pp. 1–2, for periodic mode and Fock occupations, partition product, continuum Planck spectrum, energy/entropy densities, and the stated role of wall interactions in establishing equilibrium.
